summary: Shadowed session affinity after canary abort leads to mixed-model responses for subset of tenant sessions
description:
Issue summary:
During an automated canary abort triggered by an autoscaler spike (2026-03-11 02:13 UTC) a subset of tenant sessions for KiteAnalytics began getting mixed responses: some requests hit the intended pinned variant (rwdx-3b-v2) while others were routed to the fallback quantized variant (rwdx-3b-quantized). This affected ~0.6% of active sessions for the tenant and manifested as inconsistent output for the same conversation thread.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: divergent outputs in ongoing chat sessions, occasional downstream schema deviations for structured responses.
- Scope: single tenant (KiteAnalytics), prod us-east, ~120 affected session IDs (~0.6% of tenant active sessions).
- Business impact: enterprise customer reported degraded UX; some API calls were retried by their client causing elevated token usage.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (dedicated capacity) in us-east region.
- Canary was running rwdx-3b-v2; fallback variant is rwdx-3b-quantized.
- Edge proxy version: 1.12.4. Routing coordinator: 2.8.1. Autoscaler: 4.0.0-preview

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant begins session on pinned variant (cohort cookie present, X-Redwood-Session token A).
2) Canary abort/rollback event triggered during autoscaler activity and health probe flapping.
3) Routing coordinator reconciled cohort state but the edge proxy had in-flight requests carrying both the older session token and a newly-issued session token (token B) due to a header rewrite race in our edge sidecar.
4) Some requests hashed to cohort A (pinned) and others to cohort B (fallback), producing interleaved responses in the same session thread.

Observed behavior:
- Interleaved responses from two model variants within the same session.
- Delta in tokenization length for similar prompts (indicator of different model variant).
- Datadog traces show split spans where parent request is identical but downstream routing branches to two different model backends.

Expected behavior:
- After canary abort, session affinity should be preserved or explicitly rebounded so all in-flight and subsequent requests map consistently (either fully to fallback or fully preserved to original pinned variant for the session).

Initial hypothesis:
- Edge sidecar header rewrite during the canary abort produced a transient duplicate/ambiguous session token (token A and token B) on a small percentage of requests.
- Routing coordinator accepted the abort and created new cohort bindings while edge continued to send requests hashed by stale token, creating a shadowed affinity state.
- The combination of in-flight requests + delayed cohort reconciliation caused the session hashing to flip for some requests.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Support instructed KiteAnalytics to trigger a tenant session reset (API: POST /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/session-reset) which forced a fresh session token issuance; that cleared most affected sessions within ~8 minutes.
- On our side: temporarily disabled the canary abort automation for the customer's dedicated pool and performed a manual rollback with a short drain window to avoid header rewrite races.
- Deployed a hotfix (routing-coordinator PR linked) to add a short-lived token reconciliation step on canary aborts to detect and normalize duplicate session tokens.

Next steps / follow-up:
- Engineering: add unit + integration tests for header-rewrite races (assigned to Diego Ramos, ETA 2026-03-20).
- Ops: schedule a controlled canary abort simulation in staging for the affected edge proxy and routing versions (runbook link provided).
- Product: review autoscaler probe sensitivity to reduce abort frequency during bursty traffic patterns.
- CS: provide KiteAnalytics with a post-incident summary and offer token-credit for excess retries.

Attachments / Links:
- Datadog trace samples: https://app.datadoghq.com/trace/trace_id=abcd-ef12
- Kibana logs (edge proxy): https://kibana.redwood/prod/us-east/logs?query=tenant:kiteanalytics%20\"X-Redwood-Session\"
- Routing coordinator PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-coordinator/pull/3287
- Runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Canary+Abort+Runbook

resolution_notes: Partial mitigation: session-reset workaround and hotfix deployed to routing-coordinator. Full mitigation includes integration tests and autoscaler probe adjustments. Customer credited for excess token usage; postmortem pending.
workaround: Tenant session reset via admin API (POST /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/session-reset) and temporary suspension of automated canary aborts for affected dedicated pool.
root_cause: Race between edge sidecar header rewrite and routing-coordinator cohort rebinding during an automated canary abort. In-flight requests carried ambiguous session tokens leading to split hashing across cohorts.
